extracted.intended_audience: researchers and authors submitting manuscripts to academic journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on preparing and submitting journal manuscripts so they survive editorial triage (desk review) and proceed to full peer review. Covers common causes of desk rejection and practical tips to avoid them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting a topic outside the journal scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting a topic that is outside the scope of the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represents lack of preparation by the author and typically receives desk rejection. If the topic is not ‘too far outside the scope’ and the journal belongs to a large family, the editor may suggest submitting to a sister/family journal via journal transfer/transfer cascade. Either way, the article cannot proceed further at the initial journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poorly prepared title page and abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Not preparing or presenting well the title page and abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First impressions based on the first few pages matter. Editors often give each manuscript only 3–4 minutes at initial triage. Traits that lead to quick rejection include manuscripts that look like they were quickly put together, contain spelling errors, have a vaguely worded or sloppily prepared abstract, or sport a poorly articulated or missing hypothesis statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low-quality figures and illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Including poor quality figures (low-quality images or poorly executed illustrations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and reviewers look at tables and figures soon after the title and abstract. Low-quality images or poorly executed illustrations may cause outright rejection or immediate pre-review improvement requests. Ensure images meet resolution and formatting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confusing or unclear data tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Including confusing, unclear tables which obscure or complicate data rather than make results clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables should clarify results; tables that obscure or complicate interpretation can sour editors toward a paper. Make tables clear, well-labeled, and designed to make findings accessible quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not following the journal's Information for Authors / Author Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to follow the Information for Authors (Author Guidelines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompliance with journal-specific submission rules is a common cause of desk rejection. This includes formatting, limits, and required documentation; editors expect submissions to adhere to stated policies and formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceeding article word or image count
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly exceeding the article word or image count specified by the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to word limits and image counts in the author guidelines; exceeding them signals noncompliance and may trigger desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omitting a cover letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Omitting an essential element such as the cover letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A cover letter is often required and should be prepared according to the journal's instructions; omission can be seen as incomplete submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omitting clinical trial registry information
rubrics_metrics.description: Omitting clinical trial registry information when required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trials and some prospective studies must include registry details; failing to provide them can cause immediate rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omitting Institutional Review Board (IRB) approval note
rubrics_metrics.description: Omitting a note of Institutional Review Board approval where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human-subjects research typically requires IRB/ethics approval documentation or statements; absence is a serious compliance issue and can lead to desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omitting financial disclosures of authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to include financial disclosures of authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure of funding and conflicts of interest is commonly required; omission undermines transparency and may prompt rejection or requests for correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadequate or improperly formatted references
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References should sufficiently document the literature foundation for the paper and be formatted per journal style. Poorly prepared or incomplete reference sections can result in desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorrect English language and grammar
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorrectly using English language and grammar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many otherwise-valuable papers are rejected because ideas are not phrased in proper English. If English is not the author's first language, seek a native speaker or professional editing service to improve clarity and correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit scientifically significant topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit papers that address scientifically significant topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Groundbreaking research, reports on highly relevant or significant topics, and prospective studies with large datasets and conclusive results are more likely to be reviewed. Single case reports, confirmatory studies, or inconclusive research are less likely to survive desk triage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliver a high-quality, well-prepared manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver a high-quality, well-prepared manuscript that pays attention to all details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid cosmetic, formatting, and language-usage errors. 'Sweat the details' so editors have no reason to reject the paper for surface issues; careful preparation increases chances of full peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review your paper for language before submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Review your paper for the language; use a native speaker or editing service if needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If English is not your first language and you are submitting to an English-language journal, ask a native English speaker or a professional editing service to review the manuscript prior to submission to reduce language-related rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide an adequate and properly formatted reference section
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an adequate and properly formatted reference section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sufficiently document the academic literature foundational to your paper and format references according to the journal's style. Use available reference-formatting services if needed to meet the journal's requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be professional in responding to editorial decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Be professional in your response to the journal's decision and cultivate long-term relationships with editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond without emotional reactions, learn from criticism, and show growth as an author. Professional behavior and repeatedly submitting good papers can reduce future desk rejections by building trust with editors and editorial offices.
